claims.claim_ar: تكرار الأفعال المتتابعة (آمَنُوا، هَاجَرُوا، وَجَاهَدُوا) كأسلوب موازنةٍ وتكثيفٍ للتأكيد على صفة الجماعة والقيام بالأعمال الصالحة.
claims.claim_en: The succession of verbs (آمَنُوا, هَاجَرُوا, وَجَاهَدُوا) forms parallel repetition — a balancing/enumerative device that compresses and intensifies the description of the group's faith and deeds.

claims.source_quote_ar: أُولَئِكَ اسم إشارة مبنيّ في محلّ رفع مبتدأ
claims.claim_ar: الفاء في «فَأُولَئِكَ» تعمل كأداة فصلٍ وربطٍ: تفصل النتيجة عن السياق السابق ثم تربطها به لتأكيد أن المراد من الأعمال الموصوفة هم «أُولَئِكَ» (أولئك منهم) وتقديم تمكينهم وخاصّيتهم.
claims.claim_en: The particle fa- in «fa-ulā'ika» functions to separate and then connect: it isolates the resulting statement and links it back to the preceding clause, emphasizing that the described actors are indeed 'those' (from you) and marking their special status.
claims.needs_review_reason: Interpretive: labeling the fa- here as a rhetorical device of 'separation-and-connection' is interpretive and other commentators may treat it primarily as a grammatical connective.

claims.claim_ar: بداية الجملة بـ«إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ» باستخدام «إنَّ» تؤدي دور توكيدٍ واختتامٍ مختصرٍ يختزل حكمًا عامًا في عبارة موجزة ذات قوة تقريرية.
claims.claim_en: Starting the clause with «Inna» in «Inna Allāha bikulli shay'in ʿalīm» serves an emphatic and concise closing: it compresses a general ruling into a brief, forceful declarative statement.
claims.needs_review_reason: Labeling this effect as 'ijaaz' (conciseness) is a rhetorical reading based on the particle's emphatic force; commentators may prefer a grammatical description (tawkeed) rather than the rhetorical subtype chosen.

warnings: The identification of some devices (e.g., labeling the fa- as 'fasl_wasl' or the use of 'إِنَّ' as 'ijaaz') is interpretive; alternative classifications are possible depending on the commentator's approach (grammatical vs. rhetorical).

Source quotes were taken from the supplied commentary chunks (mainly the al-Jadwal / Safi chunk). Some source fragments list forms or grammatical glosses rather than explicit rhetorical labels; the rhetorical readings above are inferred from those glosses and the ayah text.
